column1: Appendix table 7. Adults exiting parole, by type of exit, 2014
Report title: Probation and Parole in the United States, 2014   NCJ 249057
Data source: Annual Probation Survey and Annual Parole Survey
Authors:  Danielle Kaeble, Laura M. Maruschak and Thomas P. Bonczar
Appendix table 7. Adults exiting parole, by type of exit, 2014
Note: Detail may not sum to total due to rounding. Counts based on most recent data and may differ from previously published statistics. See Methodology.
a/Includes persons discharged because of release to special sentence, violations, deportations, incarceration, and revocations. Includes some early terminations and expirations of sentence.

b/Includes 2,160 parolees who were transferred to another state and 7,038 parolees who exited for other reasons. Other reasons include, but are not limited to, parolees who had a pending revocation warrant; were discharged to probation, detainer, or another criminal justice status; were deported or transferred to the jurisdiction of Immigration and Customs Enforcement; were transferred to another state through an interstate compact agreement; were pardoned; or had their sentence terminated by the court through an appeal.
c/Some or all date were estimated for type of exit.
Source: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Annual Parole Survey, 2014.
